meta.title: Fosta Studio: a small, fast, open-source database client
meta.description: Fosta Studio is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) desktop database client for Windows, with a web edition for Docker: MariaDB, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, ClickHouse and Oracle, with workspaces, SSH and TLS, a fast data grid, ER diagrams and a built-in AI agent that knows your schema.
meta.socialDescription: Free and open-source database client for 11 engines, from MariaDB and PostgreSQL to Redis, Elasticsearch and Oracle, with workspaces, SSH and TLS, safety rules and a built-in AI agent that knows your schema.
meta.ogImageAlt: Fosta Studio logo with the text: a small, fast, open-source database client

why.title: Fast where it counts, careful where it matters
why.intro: A native client for developers who move between projects, engines and environments all day, and would rather not break production on the way.
stats.label: Fosta Studio in numbers
stats.size: installer download; a portable .exe needs no install
stats.ai: AI providers, from Claude and GPT to local models
why.native.title: Native, small and quick
why.native.text: A Rust core in a Tauri 2 shell with a plain TypeScript UI and a virtualised grid. The installer is about 9 MB, and the app leaves your memory to the databases.
why.engines.title: A view that fits each engine
why.engines.text: SQL tables open in an editable grid. Redis keys, Elasticsearch search, ClickHouse parts and Oracle PL/SQL each get a view of their own instead of being squeezed into rows.
why.workspaces.title: Workspaces that open their own tunnels
why.workspaces.text: Each project or environment keeps its connections, tabs and startup tasks. Open it and kubectl port-forward starts, restarts when it drops, and stops when you quit.
why.gateway.title: Production stays read-only
why.gateway.text: Every statement, on every engine, passes one gateway with rules per workspace. A Production workspace defaults to read-only, and risky statements ask for confirmation first.
why.open.title: Open source, desktop or Docker
why.open.text: GPL-3.0, no account, no telemetry. A Windows desktop app, or a web edition that starts with one docker run.
why.ai.title: An AI agent that knows your schema
why.ai.text: Ask in plain words. The agent explores tables and relations, writes and explains queries, opens the right view and reads task logs to help you debug. Use Claude, GPT, Gemini, Fosta or a local Ollama model.
features.title: Built for the way you work with data
features.intro: From the first query of the day to the last migration check, the everyday work stays quick, visible and under your control.
query.title: A query editor that keeps up
query.text: Syntax highlighting, a formatter and completion that knows your tables and columns, for SQL, MongoDB commands and Redis. Several statements per run; each tab keeps its own session, so BEGIN…COMMIT can span runs.
query.item1: Every run lands in a searchable history that stays on your machine
query.item2: Results open in the same grid as tables, ready to filter and export
query.item3: Streaming results that show the first rows at once, and a Stop that really cancels on the server
query.caption: A query typed, run and answered in the grid (illustration).
ws.title: Workspaces and startup tasks
ws.text: Group connections, startup tasks and open tabs per project, customer or environment, then switch from the rail on the left or with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>1…9</kbd>. Tabs of other workspaces stay open.
ws.item1: Run kubectl port-forward or any command when a workspace opens
ws.item2: Automatic restart with backoff when a tunnel drops, and live logs
ws.item3: Child processes are cleaned up when the app exits
ws.shotAlt: Fosta Studio with several workspaces in the rail and the startup task log of a kubectl port-forward.
ws.caption: Each workspace brings its own connections, tasks and tabs.
grid.title: A data grid made for editing
grid.text: A virtualised grid that pages through large tables, with type badges under each column name so you always know what you are looking at.
grid.item1: Inline editing, inserts and deletes collected in a pending-changes bar
grid.item2: Apply the changes together, or discard them; a row someone else changed is a conflict, not an overwrite
grid.item4: A record panel that follows foreign keys to related rows
grid.shotAlt: The Fosta Studio data grid with column filters, type badges, an edited cell and the pending changes bar.
grid.caption: Edits wait in the pending bar until you apply them.
diagram.title: Interactive ER diagrams
diagram.text: See how a database fits together. The diagram lays itself out automatically; drag tables around, zoom in, and export the result.
diagram.shotAlt: An ER diagram of a shop database in Fosta Studio, with tables connected by foreign keys.
diagram.caption: Tables and their foreign keys, laid out for you.
ai.title: A built-in AI agent for your databases
ai.text: Ask in plain words. The agent looks up tables, columns and relations, writes and explains queries, fixes errors, and opens a table, a diagram or a new query tab for you. Every code block has Run, Insert and New tab buttons.
ai.callout: You stay in control. Run on a code block follows your workspace's safety rules, like any run of your own. The agent's own queries are read-only, and you can turn them off.
ai.item1: Bring your own model: Fosta, OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as a local Ollama
ai.item2: Your key is stored in Windows Credential Manager and requests go straight from your machine to the provider
ai.item3: It sees metadata and what you share; the optional read-only query tool can read up to 50 rows, which go to your provider
ai.disclosure: Disclosure: Fosta, the default provider, is a separate AI API service run by the author of Fosta Studio. It is listed first for convenience only; nothing in Fosta Studio requires a Fosta account, and requests only go to the provider you configure.
ai.shotAlt: The Fosta Studio assistant panel with a question, a suggested SQL query and the Insert and New tab buttons.
ai.caption: From question to a ready-to-run query in seconds.
mini.io.title: Import & export
mini.io.text: Import CSV, TSV or JSON with column mapping. Export to CSV, CSV for Excel, JSON, SQL INSERT statements or Markdown.
mini.vector.title: MariaDB vector tools
mini.vector.text: For MariaDB 11.7+: embedding search, column and index health checks, and recall of the vector index measured against exact search.
mini.conn.title: Connections, SSH and TLS
mini.conn.text: Paste a connection string for any engine. Add an SSH tunnel with a jump host or agent, and TLS with your CA, a client certificate or a pinned fingerprint. Passwords stay in Credential Manager.
mini.cell.title: Cell editor
mini.cell.text: Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> on a long value for a large editor with NULL, word wrap, and Format / Minify with validation for JSON.
engines.title: One client for the databases you actually run
engines.intro: Each engine is a native Rust driver behind one shared interface, so workspaces, safety rules and the assistant work the same everywhere, while each engine gets a view that fits its data.
engines.mysql: Stop a running query from the editor
engines.mongodb: JSON filters, Atlas URIs, inferred diagram links, commands in the query tab
engines.redis: Key browser with an editor for each data type, console with completion; also Valkey
engines.elastic: Mapping-typed grid, Dev Tools console, ES|QL and SQL
privacy.title: Your data stays yours
privacy.intro: Fosta Studio talks to your databases and to the AI provider you configure. Nothing else.
privacy.config.title: Local, portable config
privacy.config.text: Workspaces, connections and tasks live in fosta-studio.json next to the executable. No secrets are written to it.
privacy.creds.title: Windows Credential Manager
privacy.creds.text: Database passwords and AI keys are stored in the operating system's credential store, never in the config file.
privacy.telemetry.title: No telemetry, no account
privacy.telemetry.text: The app does not phone home and does not need a sign-up. It is fully usable offline with local databases.
privacy.ai.title: What the agent sees
privacy.ai.text: The model sees table and column metadata plus the editor text, errors and logs you choose to share. Statements run only when you run them. The optional read-only query tool reads up to 50 rows per query, which go to your provider; turn it off in Settings or per workspace.
privacy.gateway.title: Statement gateway
privacy.gateway.text: Every statement, on every engine, passes through one gateway with rules per workspace: Open, Guarded, Read-only or Custom. A workspace marked Production defaults to Read-only, and relaxing a rule always comes with a loud warning.
roadmap.title: Where it is heading
roadmap.intro: Planned work, roughly in order. Plans change; open an issue to discuss any of it.
roadmap.gateway.title: Engine depth
roadmap.gateway.text: Oracle without Instant Client, Redis Cluster and Sentinel, and more tools per engine.
roadmap.profiling.title: Data profiling & generation
roadmap.profiling.text: Column statistics and histograms; rule-based test data with preview before insert.
roadmap.backup.title: Backup & restore
roadmap.backup.text: Logical dumps built by the app, no external tools required.
roadmap.mongo.title: MongoDB beyond Compass
roadmap.mongo.text: A query bar with autocomplete, document views and an aggregation builder.
roadmap.servers.title: Local database servers
roadmap.servers.text: Create and run development servers without Docker or admin rights.
roadmap.web.title: Signed builds & sync
roadmap.web.text: Code-signed installers, winget and Scoop packages, and end-to-end encrypted sync between machines.
oss.title: Free software, built in the open
oss.license: Fosta Studio is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0. Use it, study it, change it and share it.
oss.cla: Contributions are welcome. On your first pull request you are asked to sign the Contributor License Agreement: you keep the copyright in your work, and the maintainer may also offer commercial licenses while the project itself stays GPL.
build.title: Build from source
build.text: Prefer to build it yourself? You need Node 20+, Rust 1.88+ and the MSVC or GNU toolchain (toolchain details).
build.result: The result is src-tauri\target\release\fosta-studio.exe. Want to try the UI first? npm run dev previews it in a browser with sample data.
